en.title: Hormuz Normalization Doubt Grows
en.summary: The probability of Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by end of June dropped 8% to 14%, driven by shipping officials' skepticism and a "most optimistic" two-month recovery projection. Despite a US-Iran agreement signed on June 17, experts indicate a much slower return to pre-war levels.
drivers: Shipping officials project 50% capacity at best.
CNBC reports "most optimistic" 2-month recovery.
Traffic "far from pre-war normals" despite picking up.
Trump team's "within a month" still past June end.
en.why_matters: Normalization is crucial for global oil supply stability and international trade, impacting energy prices and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Continued disruption poses significant economic risks.
en.bull_case: Rapid, effective implementation of the US-Iran agreement could accelerate traffic normalization beyond current expectations by month-end.
en.bear_case: Persistent security concerns and logistical hurdles, alongside shipping officials' cautious outlook, will prevent full normalization by June 30.

zh.title: 霍尔木兹海峡恢复正常存疑
zh.summary: 霍尔木兹海峡交通在六月底前恢复正常的可能性下降8%至14%，主要受航运官员的悲观预测及“最乐观”需两个月恢复的报告驱动。尽管6月17日签署了美伊协议，专家仍指出恢复至战前水平将非常缓慢。
drivers: 航运官员预计最多恢复50%运力。
CNBC称“最乐观”需两个月恢复。
交通量虽有回升但远低于战前。
特朗普团队“一月内”仍超六月底。
zh.why_matters: 交通正常化对全球石油供应稳定和国际贸易至关重要，影响能源价格及中东地缘政治紧张局势。持续中断带来显著经济风险。
zh.bull_case: 美伊协议若能迅速有效执行，有望加速交通恢复，超出当前市场预期在月底前实现正常化。
zh.bear_case: 持续的安全担忧和物流障碍，加上航运官员的谨慎展望，将阻止交通在6月30日前完全恢复正常。

en.title: Fed Rate Change Expectations Rise by July 2026
en.summary: The probability of no Fed interest rate change by July 2026 decreased by 8% to 72%. This shift was primarily driven by the latest Fed 'dot plot' revealing a hawkish stance among FOMC members and UBS's expectation of no easing this year.
drivers: Hawkish Fed 'dot plot' projections
UBS's hawkish outlook for Fed policy
en.why_matters: This movement indicates increased market anticipation of future Fed policy adjustments, impacting borrowing costs and economic growth forecasts. It signals potential shifts in monetary policy beyond initial stability.
en.bull_case: Persistent inflation moderation or economic slowdown could lead the Fed to maintain current rates longer than expected.
en.bear_case: Stronger economic data or persistent inflation could force the Fed to implement further rate hikes by July 2026.
